note: Phase 1 starter set. Every quote below was checked against a primary or clearly documented secondary source before inclusion — nothing here was generated because it 'sounded right'. Coverage is intentionally partial: only concepts/themes with quotes I could verify are included. More will be added in later passes rather than padded out now. Newer short quotes were added from memory and have NOT been re-checked online. Those with no tag name a dated book, speech or journal; those tagged 'Widely cited' are commonly attributed without a firm primary source. Check any quote before using it in an exam answer. Quotes tagged 'Wikiquote' were copied from the quote lists on Wikiquote with the citation shown there; Wikiquote is community-edited and the citation is secondary, so confirm the original before relying on a quote in an exam answer.

quotes.quote: Constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated. We must realize that our people have yet to learn it.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: Speech to the Constituent Assembly, 4 November 1948
quotes.meaning: Ambedkar warned that following a democratic constitution's forms and spirit does not come naturally to a society — it has to be consciously learned and practised.
quotes.usage: Use when a question asks about constitutional values, the gap between law and practice, or why constitutionalism needs civic education.

quotes.quote: A paramount reverence for the forms of the constitution, enforcing obedience to authority and acting under and within these forms, yet combined with the habit of open speech, of action subject only to definite legal control, and unrestrained censure of those very authorities as to all their public acts.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: Speech to the Constituent Assembly, 4 November 1948 (quoting George Grote's definition, which Ambedkar endorsed)
quotes.meaning: Defines constitutional morality as obeying constitutional forms while still retaining the right to freely criticise those in authority.
quotes.usage: Good for a body paragraph on dissent, free speech and constitutionalism coexisting.

quotes.quote: The survival of our democracy and the unity and integrity of the nation depend upon the realisation that constitutional morality is no less essential than constitutional legality. Dharma (righteousness; sense of public duty or virtue) lives in the hearts of public men; when it dies there, no Constitution, no law, no amendment, can save it.
quotes.author: Nani Palkhivala
quotes.source: Arguments in the Privy Purse case, Madhav Rao Scindia v. Union of India (1971)
quotes.meaning: Legal compliance alone cannot sustain a constitution — it depends on public servants genuinely internalising its values.
quotes.usage: Powerful complement to Ambedkar's constitutional morality quote, emphasising that law without internalised ethics is fragile.

quotes.quote: Constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated. We must realise that our people have yet to learn it.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: Speech on the Draft Constitution, Constituent Assembly of India, 4 November 1948
quotes.meaning: Respect for constitutional processes and restraint does not come naturally to a society; it must be deliberately cultivated through civic education and institutional practice.
quotes.usage: Core quote for GS4/GS2 answers on constitutional morality, rule of law, and why constitutionalism needs active nurturing.

quotes.quote: The morality that public perceives, the Constitution may not conceive of.
quotes.author: Justice Dipak Misra
quotes.source: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, (2018) 10 SCC 1, judgment dated 6 September 2018
quotes.meaning: Constitutional morality can diverge from and must override prevailing social/public morality when fundamental rights are at stake.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4/GS2 answers distinguishing constitutional morality from popular/social morality, especially on rights-based judgments.

quotes.quote: I feel that it is workable, it is flexible and it is strong enough to hold the country together both in peace time and in war time.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: Closing speech on the adoption of the Constitution, Constituent Assembly of India, 25 November 1949
quotes.meaning: Ambedkar's own assessment that the Constitution's success depends less on its text than on the men who work it and the political conduct that surrounds it.
quotes.usage: Use for GS2/GS4 answers on constitutional resilience, flexibility, and Ambedkar's final reflections before the Constitution's adoption.

quotes.quote: The survival of our democracy and the unity and integrity of the nation depend upon the realisation that constitutional morality is no less essential than constitutional legality. Dharma lives in the hearts of public men; when it dies there, no Constitution, no law, no amendment, can save it.
quotes.author: Nani Palkhivala
quotes.source: We, The People: India, The Largest Democracy
quotes.meaning: Constitutions survive only when public figures internalize constitutional morality as a lived value, not merely follow legal formalities.
quotes.usage: Use for GS2/GS4 answers on why constitutional morality (dharma in public life) matters beyond mere legal compliance.

quotes.quote: The first thing in my judgement we must do is to hold fast to constitutional methods of achieving our social and economic objectives... These methods are nothing but the Grammar of Anarchy and the sooner they are abandoned, the better for us.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: 'The Grammar of Anarchy' speech, Constituent Assembly of India, 25 November 1949
quotes.meaning: Ambedkar warns against abandoning constitutional methods for revolution, civil disobedience, or satyagraha once constitutional democracy is established, calling such methods the 'grammar of anarchy.'
quotes.usage: Widely cited for GS2/GS4 answers on constitutional methods, dissent within democracy, and the limits of extra-constitutional protest post-Independence.

quotes.quote: Any rule based on discrimination or segregation of women pertaining to biological characteristics is not only unfounded, indefensible and implausible but can also never pass the muster of constitutional morality.
quotes.author: Chief Justice Dipak Misra
quotes.source: Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala (the Sabarimala judgment), 28 September 2018
quotes.meaning: Discriminatory customs based on women's biology cannot survive scrutiny under constitutional morality, regardless of tradition.
quotes.usage: Use for GS2/GS4 answers on constitutional morality overriding discriminatory social/religious customs, especially on gender.

quotes.quote: A democracy in which the government, whomever that government may be, will be bound by a higher set of rules, embodied in a constitution, and will not be able to govern the country as it pleases.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Inaugural Address as President of South Africa, Pretoria, 10 May 1994
quotes.meaning: True constitutional democracy binds even the government itself to higher rules, preventing arbitrary rule regardless of who holds power.
quotes.usage: Use for GS2/GS4 answers on constitutionalism as a check on government power itself, not just on citizens.

quotes.quote: An honest public servant can't become rich in politics. He can only attain greatness and satisfaction by service.
quotes.author: Harry S. Truman
quotes.source: Widely documented in Truman's public remarks; commonly cited in public-service literature
quotes.meaning: Public office should be measured by service rendered, not personal enrichment.
quotes.usage: Use for questions on integrity, probity, or why public servants shouldn't use office for personal gain.

quotes.quote: Public service must be more than doing a job efficiently and honestly. It must be a complete dedication to the people and to the nation.
quotes.author: Margaret Chase Smith
quotes.source: U.S. Senator; widely documented public remarks
quotes.meaning: Competence and honesty are necessary but not sufficient — service requires genuine commitment.
quotes.usage: Useful to distinguish 'efficiency' from 'dedication' in a governance or civil-service answer.

quotes.quote: A public office is not a job, it is an opportunity to do something for the public.
quotes.author: Franklin Knight Lane
quotes.source: U.S. Secretary of the Interior; widely documented public remarks
quotes.meaning: Reframes public office as an opportunity for service rather than a career transaction.
quotes.usage: Short, quotable line — works well as an opening or closing line on the civil-services/GS4 theme.

quotes.quote: In its people decisions, management must demonstrate that it realizes that integrity is one absolute requirement of a manager.
quotes.author: Peter Drucker
quotes.source: Management: Tasks, Responsibilities, Practices (1973)
quotes.meaning: Integrity isn't one virtue among many for a manager/administrator — it's a non-negotiable baseline.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 questions on why integrity should be a threshold qualification, not just a bonus trait, in appointments and promotions.

quotes.quote: In looking for people to hire, you look for three qualities: integrity, intelligence and energy. And if they don't have the first, the other two will kill you.
quotes.author: Warren Buffett (who himself attributed the saying to an unnamed source)
quotes.source: 1987 Letter to Berkshire Hathaway Shareholders; repeated at a 1993 Columbia Business School talk
quotes.meaning: Competence without integrity is dangerous — intelligence and energy amplify the harm a dishonest person can do.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on why integrity should be the first screening criterion in appointments, not an afterthought.

quotes.quote: I tell you, do not quarrel with the instruments with which you want to work.

quotes.source: Speech to the Constituent Assembly of India defending the All India Services, 10 October 1949
quotes.meaning: Patel's defence of the civil services as the 'steel frame' of administration, urging political leaders not to undermine the bureaucratic instruments they must govern through.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on civil service neutrality, the political-bureaucratic relationship, and the value of a stable administrative steel frame.

quotes.quote: The field of administration is a field of business. It is removed from the hurry and strife of politics.
quotes.author: Woodrow Wilson
quotes.source: 'The Study of Administration', Political Science Quarterly, Vol. 2, No. 2 (1887)
quotes.meaning: Administration should be a professional, technical function insulated from partisan political interference, laying the foundation for the politics-administration dichotomy.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on civil service neutrality and the classical politics-administration dichotomy in public administration theory.

quotes.quote: You can look forward to your future with trust and confidence, and if you serve in the true spirit of service, I am sure you will have your best reward.
quotes.author: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
quotes.source: Address to the first batch of Administrative Services Officers, Metcalfe House, New Delhi, 21 April 1947
quotes.meaning: Patel's foundational address to India's first civil servants, framing genuine service (not self-interest) as the true reward of public office.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on the ethos of civil service and the spirit in which public servants should approach their role; 21 April is observed as Civil Services Day in India.

quotes.quote: I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India... and that I will duly and faithfully and to the best of my ability, knowledge and judgment perform the duties of my office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.
quotes.author: Constitution of India
quotes.source: Third Schedule, Form of Oath (for judges, ministers, and other constitutional officeholders)
quotes.meaning: The constitutionally prescribed oath binds public officeholders to faithful, impartial duty to the Constitution and the nation, free of personal bias.
quotes.usage: Direct constitutional citation for GS4 answers on the formal basis of integrity and impartiality expected of public officeholders in India.

quotes.quote: The superior man thinks of virtue; the small man thinks of comfort. The superior man thinks of the sanctions of law; the small man thinks of favours which he may receive.

quotes.meaning: Gandhi's Trusteeship doctrine: wealth and power are held in trust for society, not owned absolutely.

quotes.quote: Love and compassion are necessities, not luxuries. Without them humanity cannot survive.
quotes.author: The 14th Dalai Lama (Tenzin Gyatso)

quotes.usage: Good short line for a GS4 answer on why compassion matters in administration, not just as a personal virtue.

quotes.source: No Future Without Forgiveness (1999)

quotes.meaning: Compassion is not merely a feeling but is completed only when translated into concrete service.

quotes.quote: Compassion asks us to go where it hurts, to enter into the places of pain, to share in brokenness, fear, confusion, and anguish.

quotes.source: Discernment: Reading the Signs of Daily Life (2013)
quotes.meaning: Compassion requires actively entering into others' suffering, not observing it from a comfortable distance.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on the difference between sympathy (feeling for) and compassion (entering into another's situation).

quotes.quote: Trusteeship provides a means of transforming the present capitalist order of society into an egalitarian one.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: Harijan, 23 February 1947; Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi, Vol. 94, p. 39

quotes.quote: The very first requirement in a hospital is that it should do the sick no harm.
quotes.author: Florence Nightingale
quotes.source: Notes on Nursing: What It Is, and What It Is Not (1859)
quotes.meaning: Compassionate care begins with the basic ethical duty of non-maleficence — first, do no harm.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers linking compassion to the foundational duty of care and non-maleficence in service delivery.

quotes.quote: Ubuntu... speaks of the very essence of being human... Then you are generous, you are hospitable, you are friendly and caring and compassionate... My humanity is caught up, is inextricably bound up, in yours.

quotes.source: No Future Without Forgiveness (Doubleday, 1999), p. 31
quotes.meaning: The African philosophy of Ubuntu holds that one's own humanity is inseparable from compassion and care for others.

quotes.quote: Heavy bail from a poor man is obviously wrong. Poverty is society's malady and sympathy, not sternness, is the judicial response.

quotes.quote: I can do no other than be reverent before everything that is called life. I can do no other than to have compassion for all that is called life. That is the beginning and the foundation of all ethics.

quotes.source: The Teaching of Reverence for Life (1966)
quotes.meaning: Reverence for all life is the necessary foundation from which compassion, and ethics itself, must begin.

quotes.author: Aristotle

quotes.usage: Use for GS4 questions distinguishing courage from recklessness, e.g. in whistleblowing or crisis-decision case studies.

quotes.quote: Far better it is to dare mighty things, to win glorious triumphs, even though checkered by failure, than to take rank with those poor spirits who neither enjoy much nor suffer much, because they live in the gray twilight that knows not victory nor defeat.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: 'Citizenship in a Republic' address, the Sorbonne, Paris, 23 April 1910 (often called 'The Man in the Arena')

quotes.usage: Strong for GS4/essay answers on social justice, discrimination, or why administrators can't treat injustice elsewhere as 'not their problem'.

quotes.quote: Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought. A theory however elegant and economical must be rejected or revised if it is untrue; likewise laws and institutions no matter how efficient and well-arranged must be reformed or abolished if they are unjust.
quotes.author: John Rawls
quotes.source: A Theory of Justice (1971)
quotes.meaning: Justice is a non-negotiable baseline for institutions — efficiency or elegance cannot excuse injustice.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 questions weighing efficiency/administrative convenience against fairness and justice.

quotes.quote: Act in such a way that you treat humanity, whether in your own person or in the person of another, always at the same time as an end and never simply as a means.
quotes.author: Immanuel Kant
quotes.source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785) — the 'Humanity Formula' of the Categorical Imperative
quotes.meaning: People must never be used merely as tools/instruments for someone else's purpose — they have inherent worth.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 questions on treating citizens/subordinates as ends in themselves, e.g. in welfare delivery or bureaucratic decision-making.

quotes.quote: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.
quotes.author: United Nations
quotes.source: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 1 (1948)
quotes.meaning: Establishes equal dignity and rights as the foundational premise of all human rights.
quotes.usage: Foundational quote for essays or GS4 answers on justice, equality, or human rights.

quotes.quote: Justice is when everyone minds his own business, and refrains from meddling in others' affairs.
quotes.author: Plato
quotes.source: Republic, Book IV, 433a (a provisional definition within the dialogue, not Plato's final word on justice)
quotes.meaning: An early definition in the Republic: justice as each person/class performing its proper role without overreach.
quotes.usage: Use to introduce classical definitions of justice before contrasting with modern theories like Rawls's.

quotes.quote: Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
quotes.source: Letter from Birmingham Jail, 16 April 1963
quotes.meaning: Injustice against any group threatens the entire fabric of justice, since all communities are interconnected.
quotes.usage: Powerful opening/closing line for GS4 or essay answers on justice, solidarity, and civic responsibility toward others' suffering.

quotes.quote: Each person possesses an inviolability founded on justice that even the welfare of society as a whole cannot override.
quotes.author: John Rawls
quotes.source: A Theory of Justice (Harvard University Press, 1971)
quotes.meaning: Individual rights and justice are inviolable and cannot be sacrificed merely for aggregate social welfare, grounding Rawls's justice-as-fairness framework.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on distributive justice, individual rights versus utilitarian calculus, or Rawlsian justice as fairness.

quotes.quote: Freedom means the supremacy of human rights everywhere.
quotes.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
quotes.source: State of the Union Address to Congress ('The Four Freedoms' speech), 6 January 1941
quotes.meaning: True freedom and justice require the universal supremacy of human rights, not their selective application.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4/essay answers linking justice, freedom, and universal human rights, citing a foundational 20th-century human rights speech.

quotes.quote: If a theory of justice is to guide reasoned choice of policies, strategies or institutions, then the identification of fully just social arrangements is neither necessary nor sufficient.
quotes.author: Amartya Sen
quotes.source: The Idea of Justice (Allen Lane / Harvard University Press, 2009)
quotes.meaning: Sen argues justice theory should focus on comparing and reducing real injustices rather than fixating on an ideal, perfectly just social arrangement (a critique of Rawlsian 'transcendental institutionalism').
quotes.usage: Use for advanced GS4 answers contrasting Sen's comparative approach to justice with Rawls's ideal-theory approach.

quotes.quote: To deny people their human rights is to challenge their very humanity.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Address to a Joint Session of the United States Congress, 26 June 1990
quotes.meaning: Denying someone's fundamental human rights is not a minor legal violation but an assault on their basic humanity.
quotes.usage: Powerful opening line for GS4/essay answers on justice, human rights, and the dehumanizing effect of rights denial.

quotes.quote: We who seek justice will have to do justice to others.

quotes.quote: The whole idea of revenge and punishment is a childish day-dream.

quotes.quote: Murder is sometimes punished, free speech always.

quotes.usage: Use to open a GS4 answer on why emotional intelligence matters alongside technical competence in administration.

quotes.quote: Anyone can become angry — that is easy. But to be angry with the right person, to the right degree, at the right time, for the right purpose, and in the right way — this is not easy.
quotes.author: Aristotle (popular rendering of ideas from Book II of the Nicomachean Ethics)

quotes.meaning: Emotional regulation isn't suppressing emotion but directing it appropriately — the right target, intensity, timing and manner.

quotes.quote: Self-awareness — recognizing a feeling as it happens — is the keystone of emotional intelligence.
quotes.author: Daniel Goleman
quotes.source: Emotional Intelligence: Why It Can Matter More Than IQ (1995)
quotes.meaning: All other emotional-intelligence skills build on the basic ability to notice one's own feelings as they occur.
quotes.usage: Use to open a GS4 answer on emotional intelligence, establishing self-awareness as the foundational skill.

quotes.quote: If your emotional abilities aren't in hand, if you don't have self-awareness, if you are not able to manage your distressing emotions, if you can't have empathy and have effective relationships, then no matter how smart you are, you are not going to get very far.
quotes.author: Daniel Goleman
quotes.source: Emotional Intelligence: Why It Can Matter More Than IQ (Bantam Books, 1995), p. xi (Preface)
quotes.meaning: Intellectual ability alone is insufficient for real-world effectiveness without self-awareness, emotional regulation, and interpersonal skill.
quotes.usage: Strong opening/closing line for GS4 answers on why EQ matters alongside IQ in public administration.

quotes.quote: Emotional intelligence refers to the capacity for recognising our own feelings and those of others, for motivating ourselves, and for managing emotions well in ourselves and in our relationships.
quotes.author: Daniel Goleman
quotes.source: Working with Emotional Intelligence (Bantam Books, 1998)
quotes.meaning: A working definition of EI as self-awareness, self-motivation, and relationship management combined.
quotes.usage: Use as a crisp definitional line for GS4 answers introducing or defining emotional intelligence.

quotes.quote: A type of social intelligence that involves the ability to monitor one's own and others' emotions, to discriminate among them, and to use the information to guide one's thinking and actions.
quotes.author: Peter Salovey and John D. Mayer
quotes.source: 'Emotional Intelligence', Imagination, Cognition and Personality, Vol. 9, No. 3 (1990)
quotes.meaning: The original academic definition of emotional intelligence, predating and underlying Goleman's later popularization of the term.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers that want to cite the original scholarly source/definition of emotional intelligence rather than its popular treatment.

quotes.quote: The cluster of abilities that help us perceive, understand, and manage emotions in ourselves and in relationships with others.

quotes.meaning: A working definition of emotional-social intelligence as a cluster of abilities spanning self-perception, understanding, and relationship management.
quotes.usage: Use as an alternative definitional citation for EI, alongside Goleman and Salovey/Mayer, drawing on the Bar-On EQ-i model.

quotes.quote: Researchers have found that even more than IQ, your emotional awareness and ability to handle feelings will determine your success and happiness in all walks of life, including family relationships.

quotes.source: Raising an Emotionally Intelligent Child (Simon & Schuster, 1997)
quotes.meaning: Emotional awareness and regulation shape life outcomes and relationship success more than raw cognitive intelligence.

quotes.quote: So, we deny ourselves — and one another — permission to feel. We toughen up, squash it down, behave irrationally.

quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on why suppressing emotions undermines, rather than strengthens, emotional intelligence.

quotes.quote: To be angry with the right person, and to the right degree, and at the right time, and for the right purpose, and in the right way — this is not for every one, nor is it easy.

quotes.meaning: Well-regulated emotional response — not the absence of emotion, but its precise calibration — is the mark of genuine emotional mastery.

quotes.quote: Karmanḇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana — You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions.

quotes.source: Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 47
quotes.meaning: One's moral duty is to act rightly and diligently, without attachment to or anxiety over the outcome — the essence of nishkama karma.
quotes.usage: Canonical quote for GS4 answers on duty, detachment from results, and the civil servant's obligation to act despite uncertain outcomes.

quotes.quote: Duty is the necessity to act out of reverence for the law.
quotes.author: Immanuel Kant
quotes.source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785)
quotes.meaning: A truly moral act is done from a sense of duty/respect for moral law itself, not from inclination or self-interest.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on deontological duty and acting from principle rather than personal benefit.

quotes.quote: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt (crediting Squire Bill Widener of Widener's Valley, Virginia)
quotes.source: Theodore Roosevelt, An Autobiography (1913), Chapter IX
quotes.meaning: Fulfilling one's duty means acting responsibly within one's present means and circumstances, not waiting for ideal conditions.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on practical duty-fulfillment and making the most of available resources and authority.

quotes.quote: Freedom is only part of the story and half of the truth. Freedom is but the negative aspect of the whole phenomenon whose positive aspect is responsibleness.
quotes.author: Viktor E. Frankl
quotes.source: Man's Search for Meaning (1946; English translation 1959)
quotes.meaning: Freedom without responsibility is incomplete; true freedom is only meaningful when paired with taking responsibility for how it is exercised.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers linking freedom and responsibility, especially on the duties that accompany rights and liberties.

quotes.quote: Act in such a way that you treat humanity, whether in your own person or in the person of any other, never merely as a means to an end, but always at the same time as an end.
quotes.author: Immanuel Kant
quotes.source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785) — the Humanity Formulation of the Categorical Imperative
quotes.meaning: Moral duty requires treating every person as inherently valuable in themselves, never merely as an instrument for someone else's purposes.
quotes.usage: Core citation for GS4 answers on deontological duty, human dignity, and the categorical imperative's humanity formulation.

quotes.quote: Never shirk the proper dispatch of your duty, no matter if you are freezing or hot, groggy or well-rested, vilified or praised, not even if dying or pressed by other demands.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Meditations, Book 6, Section 2
quotes.meaning: Duty must be performed consistently regardless of personal circumstance, mood, or external judgment.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 answers on unwavering commitment to duty despite personal hardship or distraction.

quotes.quote: The true source of rights is duty.

quotes.source: Young India, 8 January 1925
quotes.meaning: Rights are not free-standing entitlements; they flow from and are grounded in the faithful performance of duty.
quotes.usage: Concise, widely cited line for GS4 answers on the relationship between rights and duties in public and civic life.

quotes.quote: Civilization is that mode of conduct which points out to man the path of duty.

quotes.quote: It is not often that a generation is challenged, as we today are challenged.

quotes.quote: Artificial intelligence is likely to be either the best or worst thing to happen to humanity.
quotes.author: Stephen Hawking

quotes.meaning: Frames AI as a genuine double-edged development, not simply progress or simply danger.
quotes.usage: Strong opening line for a technology/AI essay — sets up a balanced two-sided argument.

quotes.quote: We need to be super careful with AI. Potentially more dangerous than nukes.
quotes.author: Elon Musk
quotes.source: Public statement, widely reported, 2014
quotes.meaning: A blunt warning about the scale of risk unregulated AI development could pose.
quotes.usage: Use to introduce the 'risk/regulation' dimension of a technology essay.

quotes.quote: It is the scientific approach, the adventurous yet critical temper of science, the search for truth and new knowledge, the refusal to accept anything without testing and trial, the capacity to change previous conclusions in the face of new evidence, the reliance on observed fact and not pre-conceived theory.
quotes.author: Jawaharlal Nehru
quotes.source: The Discovery of India (1946) — the passage that popularised the term 'scientific temper'
quotes.meaning: Defines the scientific temper as a willingness to test, question and revise beliefs in light of evidence.
quotes.usage: Use to broaden a technology essay into 'scientific temper' more generally — good for questions on rationality, evidence-based policy, or Article 51A(h) (duty to develop scientific temper).

quotes.quote: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
quotes.author: Constitution of India
quotes.source: Article 51A(h), Fundamental Duties (inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976)
quotes.meaning: Developing scientific temper is a constitutional duty of every Indian citizen, not merely a scientific or educational aspiration.
quotes.usage: Use to ground a technology/rationality essay in the actual constitutional text, pairing well with Nehru's 'scientific temper' passage.

quotes.quote: I've always thought of AI as the most profound technology humanity is working on — more profound than fire or electricity or anything that we've done in the past.

quotes.meaning: Places AI among the most transformative technologies in human history, underscoring the scale of its likely impact.
quotes.usage: Use to establish the stakes of an AI essay before discussing its risks or governance.

quotes.quote: I think the development of full artificial intelligence could spell the end of the human race.
quotes.author: Stephen Hawking
quotes.source: BBC interview, December 2014
quotes.meaning: Unchecked, self-improving AI could outpace and eventually endanger humanity.
quotes.usage: Strong cautionary line for essays on AI risk/regulation; often paired with a counterpoint on AI's benefits for balance.

quotes.quote: I believe in the potential of this technology to transform people's lives for the better... but we will not put the world in harm's way to get there.
quotes.author: Sam Altman
quotes.source: Fortune interview, September 2026
quotes.meaning: AI's transformative potential must be pursued without compromising safety or risking large-scale harm.
quotes.usage: Use for essays on balancing AI innovation with safety and responsible deployment.

quotes.quote: The ability to make connections across disciplines — arts and sciences, humanities and technology — is a key to innovation, imagination, and genius.

quotes.source: The Moment of Lift: How Empowering Women Changes the World (2019)
quotes.meaning: Genuine technological innovation comes from bridging disciplines, not from technology in isolation.
quotes.usage: Use for essays on interdisciplinary innovation and the human dimensions of technological progress.

quotes.quote: Technology isn't bad. If you know what you want in life, technology can help you get it. But if you don't know what you want in life, it will be all too easy for technology to shape your aims for you and take control of your life.

quotes.meaning: Technology is neutral; its impact depends on whether the user has clear self-knowledge and purpose, or lets technology dictate their goals.
quotes.usage: Use for essays on technology's dual nature and the importance of human agency and self-knowledge in the digital age.

quotes.quote: The best way to understand it emotionally is we are like somebody who has this really cute tiger cub. Unless you can be very sure that it's not gonna want to kill you when it's grown up, you should worry.

quotes.source: 'We Should All Be Feminists', TEDxEuston talk, London, December 2012
quotes.meaning: Culture is a human construction and can be deliberately reshaped to secure full equality for women.
quotes.usage: Powerful line for essays on gender equality, cultural change, and challenging patriarchal norms as social constructs.

quotes.quote: Race discrimination was immediately perceived as evil, as odious, as wrong, as intolerable. But the response I was getting from the judges before whom I appeared when I first talked about sex-based discrimination... was: 'What are you talking about?'
quotes.author: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
quotes.source: U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee confirmation hearing, 1993
quotes.meaning: Gender discrimination historically took much longer than race discrimination to be recognized by courts as a serious legal wrong.
quotes.usage: Use for essays on the history/pace of legal recognition of gender discrimination and the fight for equal treatment under law.

quotes.quote: Unless and until you give to your women all those equal privileges that form the highest and noblest teaching of your great nation-builder... you will not attain that regeneration of your race.
quotes.author: Sarojini Naidu
quotes.source: Speech delivered days after the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference, Poona (archived in the Speaking While Female Speech Bank)
quotes.meaning: A nation or community cannot achieve true renewal or progress while denying women equal rights and privileges.

quotes.quote: I am those 66 million girls who are deprived of education. And today I am not raising my voice, it is the voice of those 66 million girls.

quotes.quote: Simply put, feminism is a movement to end sexism, sexist exploitation, and oppression.
quotes.author: bell hooks
quotes.source: Feminism Is for Everybody: Passionate Politics (South End Press, 2000)
quotes.meaning: A concise, accessible definition of feminism as a movement against sexist oppression, not against men or in favor of female superiority.
quotes.usage: Use as a clear definitional citation for essays introducing or clarifying the aims of feminism.

quotes.quote: Arguing that you don't care about the right to privacy because you have nothing to hide is no different than saying you don't care about free speech because you have nothing to say.
quotes.author: Edward Snowden
quotes.source: Widely documented public remarks/interview
quotes.meaning: Rebuts the 'nothing to hide' argument by comparing privacy to free speech — both are rights worth defending regardless of whether you currently need to exercise them.
quotes.usage: Strong for essays on surveillance, data privacy, or digital-age civil liberties.

quotes.quote: It was one of those pictures which are so contrived that the eyes follow you about when you move. BIG BROTHER IS WATCHING YOU... You had to live — did live, from habit that became instinct — in the assumption that every sound you made was overheard, and, except in darkness, every moment scrutinized.
quotes.author: George Orwell
quotes.source: Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949)
quotes.meaning: A fictional but enduringly influential depiction of total state surveillance eliminating any private sphere.
quotes.usage: Classic literary reference for essays on surveillance, privacy, or the psychological effect of being constantly watched.

quotes.quote: The Constitution recognizes human dignity as intrinsic to liberty; privacy attaches to the person and is an essential facet of human dignity.
quotes.author: Justice D. Y. Chandrachud
quotes.source: K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) — the Supreme Court's nine-judge bench judgment recognising privacy as a fundamental right
quotes.meaning: Grounds the right to privacy directly in human dignity, not merely as a residual or subsidiary right.
quotes.usage: Essential citation for essays or GS4/GS2 answers on the right to privacy, data protection, or the Puttaswamy judgment.

quotes.quote: Your rights matter, because you never know when you're going to need them.
quotes.author: Edward Snowden
quotes.source: TED2014 talk, 'Here's how we take back the Internet'
quotes.meaning: Rights like privacy should be protected proactively, not only once their absence is acutely felt.
quotes.usage: Short line for essays on why privacy protections matter even for those who feel they have 'nothing to hide'.

quotes.quote: Privacy is the constitutional core of human dignity.
quotes.author: Justice D. Y. Chandrachud
quotes.source: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India, judgment dated 24 August 2017
quotes.meaning: The Supreme Court frames privacy not as a mere legal technicality but as foundational to human dignity under the Constitution.
quotes.usage: Strong anchor line for essays on privacy, data protection, and digital rights, citing India's landmark privacy judgment.

quotes.quote: BIG BROTHER IS WATCHING YOU.
quotes.author: George Orwell
quotes.source: Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949), Part One, Chapter 1
quotes.meaning: A totalitarian state's constant surveillance is used to control and intimidate its citizens into compliance.
quotes.usage: Classic literary citation for essays on mass surveillance, state overreach, or loss of privacy in the digital age.

quotes.quote: Arguing that you don't care about privacy because you have nothing to hide is no different than saying you don't care about free speech because you have nothing to say.

quotes.source: Reddit AMA, 21 May 2015
quotes.meaning: The 'nothing to hide' argument against privacy rights is fallacious, just as dismissing free speech for having 'nothing to say' would be.

quotes.quote: Overcoming poverty is not a gesture of charity. It is the protection of a fundamental human right, the right to dignity and a decent life.

quotes.meaning: Reframes poverty alleviation as a rights-based obligation, not optional generosity.
